installation.note: ping is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: ping sends ICMP echo requests to network hosts and measures response time. It's the primary tool for testing network connectivity, checking if a host is reachable, and diagnosing network issues. ping continues sending packets until stopped (Ctrl+C).

syntax.description: Send ICMP packets to HOST (IP address or hostname). Continues until stopped with Ctrl+C. Shows round-trip time and packet loss.

options.use_case: Send only 4 packets then stop (instead of continuous)
Send packets every 2 seconds (default is 1 second)
Wait 5 seconds for response before timing out
Send larger packets (useful for testing MTU)
Show only summary statistics, not each packet

misconceptions.title: ping shows download speed
misconceptions.reality: ping shows latency (round-trip time), not bandwidth/speed. Low ping = low latency (good for gaming, real-time). High ping = high latency (slower response).
misconceptions.tip: ping = latency (response time), not speed. Use speedtest-cli or similar for bandwidth testing.

misconceptions.title: ping works without internet
misconceptions.misconception: ping works on local network without internet
misconceptions.reality: ping works on local network too - you can ping local IPs (192.168.x.x) without internet. ping tests network connectivity, not just internet.
misconceptions.tip: ping works on local network. ping 192.168.1.1 tests router connectivity without internet.

common_pitfalls.solution: Press Ctrl+C to stop ping. Or use -c flag to send specific number of packets.
Ping times vary. <50ms is excellent, <100ms is good, <200ms is acceptable. Very high (>500ms) may indicate network issues.

best_practices: Use ping -c 4 for quick connectivity tests
Use ping to test both hostnames and IP addresses
Use ping to verify DNS resolution (hostname resolves to IP)
Check packet loss - 0% is ideal, >5% may indicate problems
Use ping -q for cleaner output in scripts
Press Ctrl+C to stop continuous ping
Use ping to test local network (192.168.x.x) and internet (8.8.8.8, google.com)
performance_tips: Use -c to limit packets for faster tests

additional_notes.latency_vs_speed: ping shows latency (response time), not bandwidth. Low ping = fast response, not fast download speed.
additional_notes.stopping: ping runs until Ctrl+C. Use -c flag to send specific number of packets and stop automatically.
additional_notes.common_use: Very common: ping google.com (test internet), ping -c 4 host (quick test), ping 192.168.1.1 (test router)
additional_notes.packet_loss: 0% packet loss is ideal. >5% may indicate network problems. Check statistics after stopping ping.
